Tools for driving radiatR from an AI agent

Source: R/agent_tools.R
radiatR_tools.Rd

Returns a set of ellmer::tool() definitions that let a language model run a radiatR analysis: load tracks or a table of headings, derive headings, summarise, test and plot. Register them with an ellmer chat, or serve them to an MCP client such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop with the mcptools package.

Usage

radiatR_tools()

Value

A named list of ellmer tool definitions.

Details

Each call to radiatR_tools() creates its own private session. Objects are referred to by handles ("tracks_1", "headings_1"); every result includes the R code that produced it, and the radiatR_export_script tool returns the whole session as one script that reproduces the data objects and result tables exactly.

The tools do not fill in what was left unsaid: the time type, the unit of any angle column, the convention of a table of angles, and a seed for heading derivation and for every test must be stated. A missing or invalid argument is an error rather than a default, and so is an argument the call would ignore. Some things are still chosen rather than stated: load_tracks reads a file as read_tracks() does, sniffing its delimiter and decimal mark, reading date-times as UTC, and taking a dialect's defaults (such as which body parts make up the position); it refuses a workbook with more than one sheet. Warnings and printed output are returned to the model in the result instead of being written to the console, and an error message carries the condition class, the failing call, and anything raised before the failure.

Serving over MCP

claude mcp add radiatR -- Rscript -e \
  'mcptools::mcp_server(tools = radiatR::radiatR_tools(), session_tools = FALSE)'

session_tools = FALSE keeps every call in the server process, where the handles live. Handles therefore cannot be inspected from another R console; the exported script is the bridge. Anything R prints at startup corrupts the MCP stream: in a project that uses renv, set RENV_CONFIG_SYNCHRONIZED_CHECK=FALSE for the server.

Examples

tools <- radiatR_tools()
names(tools)
#>  [1] "list_options"    "load_tracks"     "load_headings"   "derive_headings"
#>  [5] "describe"        "summarise"       "test_uniformity" "compare_groups" 
#>  [9] "plot"            "export_script"
